display: Year 3 primary school teacher in Brunswick, Melbourne. I run the school veggie garden, play wing defence in a Thursday night netball team, and am training for my first half marathon.

signals.text: The school veggie garden is in its spring planting window (peas, broad beans, lettuce) and the beans need staking.
I'm running a garden working bee on 11 October and could use extra hands, tools and plants.
I'm training for my first half marathon on 8 November. My long runs are up to 16–18 km along the Merri Creek.
My right glute is a 'lazy tyrant' and I've lost a couple of toenails. I'd happily take tips from runners on recovery and kit.
The garden's funding runs out in December, and I need a grant application drafted by early October and submitted by mid-October.
I'm stuck on the grant writing. I keep producing mug-slogan sentences and need concrete evidence like harvest numbers, kid participation and testimonials.
My grandmother's 1950s Singer treadle machine jams on nearly every stitch. I've taken it apart twice and still can't tell if it's dust, a bent part or my own incompetence.
I want to make a patchwork quilt on the Singer for a new baby in the family. Right now I mostly need a miracle.
My nana said her husband used to oil the Singer 'with a feather', and I don't know what that means.
I have a half-finished set of cushion covers and I'm a beginner at sewing.
My partner has spent nine weekends tiling our bathroom and it's going badly, and I'm quietly looking for rescue options.
I'd like more headspace. I only get weekends for projects, and I end up planning seeds during staff meetings.

offers.text: Eleven years of primary teaching (six at Brunswick Primary). I can design hands-on lessons for ages 7–10, explain things simply, and manage a room of excited kids.

I've built and run a school veggie garden with twelve raised beds and about forty kids across three year levels. I can advise on how to start one, assign roles by year level, and run a worm farm and compost.
I can host or plan a school garden visit, or share the garden's setup, planting calendar and kid-friendly activities with other teachers or schools.
I play wing defence (intercepts, pressure, loud encouragement) and could help a team that needs a defender or a training partner. My Thursday-night team is top of the ladder.
I can run with first-time half-marathon runners on weekends along the Merri Creek and swap training-plan notes.
I'm good at making kids care about plants, for example by naming every tomato and giving Gandalf a ribbon-topped staff. I can share ways to make science and gardening playful.
I can offer a teacher's view on school grant applications: what a school can actually evidence, and what kids and parents need from a funded program.
I've got a pair of Year 3 to Year 5 garden teams and a reliable parent volunteer network that can host working bees.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a vintage sewing machine hobbyist (or repair person). I fix old Singer treadle machines and bobbin-case problems and like helping beginners get a family machine running again.
catchers.can: Rachel could bring her grandmother's 1950s Singer for a weekend look or a video call, and in return offer a thank-you through the garden or a school visit.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to diagnose and fix bobbin-case jams on pre-1960 Singer treadle machines (not just modern electronic ones)?

catchers.hypo: I've written a few community or school garden grants. Would you like a second pair of eyes on your draft before it goes in?
catchers.can: Rachel could share her draft and get feedback on concrete evidence (numbers, harvest, testimonials) before submitting.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally written or reviewed a successful grant for a school or community garden program (Australian, small-scale)?

catchers.hypo: I'm a teacher at another school thinking of starting a veggie garden with a class. Where do I begin with beds, roles, funding and kids?
catchers.can: Rachel can explain her setup, share the year-level role split (tomatoes, herbs, compost), and possibly host a visit on a weekend.
catchers.confirm: Are you a teacher, or a staff member at a school, who actually wants to start or expand a student-run garden?

catchers.hypo: I'm training for my first half marathon and I'm nervous about the long runs. Does anyone around Brunswick want a running buddy?
catchers.can: Rachel can run with a first-timer on weekends along the Merri Creek and swap tips on physio, recovery and race-day planning.
catchers.confirm: Are you a first-time or early half-marathon runner who can run on weekends around Melbourne's inner north?

catchers.hypo: I'm a tiler or renovator who loves rescuing DIY bathroom projects before they get worse. I'd gladly give advice on grout, angles and setting out.
catchers.can: Rachel's partner Tom is mid-way through DIY-tiling a bathroom and could take a weekend consultation, with Rachel as the go-between.
catchers.confirm: Are you a qualified tiler (or an experienced renovator) who is willing to advise on, or step in to fix, an amateur tiling job in Melbourne?

catchers.hypo: My grandmother is in aged care and her long-term memory is vivid while her present-day memory is fading. How do you stay connected with her?
catchers.can: Rachel can share what she's learned from visiting her own nana in aged care in Preston, and swap stories and ideas.
catchers.confirm: Is the person you're caring about a grandparent in aged care whose memory is changing, and are you looking for peer support rather than medical advice?

catchers.hypo: We run a local seed library, nursery or compost group in Melbourne and would love to support a school garden with seedlings or donations.
catchers.can: Rachel could take seedlings, seeds or compost materials for the school beds and invite you to a working bee or a class visit.
catchers.confirm: Can you donate or supply spring seedlings, seeds or compost to a school garden in the Brunswick area?

catchers.hypo: I make patchwork quilts and run a small beginners' sewing circle on weekends. Would you like to join, or bring your half-finished projects?
catchers.can: Rachel could come with her half-finished cushion covers and her quilt plan, and learn pattern and piecing basics.
catchers.confirm: Do you teach or host beginner quilting or sewing sessions on weekends in Melbourne?

forbids.text: I can't do anything on weekdays during school hours, so it needs to be weekends.
I can't attend anything on Thursday nights (netball).
I can't take on anything that conflicts with the mid-October grant deadline or the 8 November half marathon.
I won't share photos or personal details of the students.
I want to repair my nana's Singer rather than replace it, so I'm not looking to swap it for a new machine.

projects.name: School veggie garden
projects.text: A twelve-bed school garden in Brunswick run by about forty students across Years 3 to 5. It needs a new funding application, weekend working bees and ongoing volunteers.

projects.name: Grandma's Singer and the baby quilt
projects.text: Revive a 1950s Singer treadle machine and use it to make a patchwork quilt for a family baby.

policy.t1: When there's a real spark I'll share the garden's funding status and grant needs, the Singer's problem, and the quilt plan.
policy.t2: Once trust is high and the other person is clear, I'll share my worries about Nana and the pressure of the grant writing.
policy.never: My finances, and any details about my sister's pregnancy.
